column8: Tue 17 Nov: store, colour for 3a: art. 709-1 read at source defines the hui as payouts resting on others' future contributions; Taiwan law is out of scope (case l.169), so never a plan step; row 3 is the stronger use.
Tue 17 Nov: store guard: added in 1999, in force in 2000 (presidential order and Lee and Li read); corrects H4-051's codified in 2000 wherever a date is printed.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3.0, one clause at most: the statute's own reason says a hui rests on the organiser's credit and the members' good faith, the dependence IPS l.11 rules out; in words, no fourth figure in 3a; the IPS's own default clause stays where l.11 has it.
Tue 17 Nov: store, colour for 3a: art. 709-9 shares a shortfall among the unpaid and names who owes it but cannot create the money; good judge line, Taiwan law out of scope.

Tue 17 Nov: store: art. 709-7 at source with its reason (the organiser has the first pot interest-free, so pays in for missing members); stronger than H4-051 and H2-083; never confuse with Q11e's founder pays first.
Tue 17 Nov: store, guard for claims 2 and 3: the legislature's own phrase, to curb the tide of hui collapses, and natural persons only, so no co-sponsor institution was ever a member.
Tue 17 Nov: store, feeds row 40: art. 709-3 made a signed hui sheet compulsory because fake bids and invented members were quite serious; a signed list proves who promised, not that money exists.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: art. 709-8 locks members in; liquidity is not the ten's point and the plan's exits are IPS l.17's two, so it serves no part.
Tue 17 Nov: store, Taiwan legal history: before 1999 a member's claim ran against the organiser alone (63台上1159 via two official pages, precedent text not read).
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d guard: the hui peaked in the 1980s and today's young do not know the word, so claim 3 weakens with the reader's age; a court column's round figures.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3.0, store first: 68% joined and 39% of them had one collapse (Jou 2003, 534 adults, 44% response, urban-weighted); about 1 in 4 is Keel arithmetic; a fourth figure breaks 3a's density cut, so words or 3.0 only.
Tue 17 Nov: store: collapses fell on few people and were mostly absorbed, not pursued (Jou 2003 p. 4), which is what resting on good faith means in practice; same sample limits as row 11.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: why people joined in 2003 (saving 52%); serves no part beyond row 11's context.
Tue 17 Nov: store only, cite only as Jou 2003's review: Wu 1980, Lin 1985 and the 1985 and 1999 provincial surveys were not read at source.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d background only: participation highest among high-income households (Levenson and Besley 1996 abstract, 1977-1991 data); never a claim that funders' boards know the hui or hear l.11 a certain way.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: roscas funded durables in Taiwan 1977-1991 (abstracts); fridges and motorbikes, not buildings.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a 1987 CIER survey treated hui as household balance-sheet credit; its results not read.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a popular history column on what hui paid for (schooling, property, businesses); no data.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d guard beside row 10: hui are fewer and many born in the 1980s never joined (CTS 2016); the NT$10bn flow is unsourced in the report, never print it.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a June 2026 Taoyuan collapse, allegations under investigation and victims' estimates; never as fact and never name the organiser.
Tue 17 Nov: store, pairs with row 37: the basic failure, members already paid stop paying and those still waiting carry the loss (Kaohsiung 1952, as reprinted).
Tue 17 Nov: store only, cite through Jou 2003: the 1983 Executive Yuan directives were not read at source.
Tue 17 Nov: store only, cite through Jou 2003: the Investigation Bureau's average loss figures were not read at source.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: two dated 1998 collapses from photo captions; colour beside rows 21 and 25.
Tue 17 Nov: store: organisers borrowed at 24% to keep their hui paying (Hsinchu judgment, 2000), a payout resting on fresh outside money until it stopped; one fraud case.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a civil servant's fake bids among colleagues, from an adapted ethics-office summary, not the judgment.
Tue 17 Nov: store, pairs with row 37: the member paid last is most exposed and here could not even prove the claim (Tainan small-claims judgment, 2004, read in part).
Tue 17 Nov: store only: a 1995 article titled the hui-collapse storm; record only, a dating sign beside row 6.
Tue 17 Nov: guard for any Taiwan hui sentence: the big chained collapses were mainland China's, from a secondary wiki; never cite them as Taiwan's and never tie the hui to Laura.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3e or 2.1 colour: the 1985 Tenth Credit run (Time) shows a licensed deposit can rest on others' conduct; the owned-not-owed reserve (Q72) already carries the custody point.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: the curb market met about 35% of private credit in 1985 (CSM, figure unsourced in the article).
Tue 17 Nov: store, beside the 3e reserve nobody can run on the plan: the 1985 panic spread across institutions until state banks took over (abstract); a Taiwan run, not a hui.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: Taiwan's late-1980s Ponzi-shaped company paying old debts with new; H5-149 holds Ponzi himself; not a hui.
Tue 17 Nov: store only, beside row 33: the 1989 Taichung collapses and the money-in-exceeds-money-out model; an author's estimates.
Tue 17 Nov: store: economics agrees with the statute that a rosca stands on members' continued good behaviour (Anderson, Baland and Moene 2009); Kenyan data, theory.

Tue 17 Nov: guard for 3a and 3d: retires H4-051's a hui whose organiser is the US Treasury, which inverts l.11 (art. 709-2 organisers are natural persons; a hui is dependence on others' money); the lead marks H4-051 refuse.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a aha candidate for a cold test, not yet the spine: the hui's last payee is owed by the most people, the ladder's 2042 rests on the same one issuer as 2033 (3.125% Nov 2041 bond, NUMBERS 0); keep NUMBERS 2's guard and gloss the hui for a US judge.

Tue 17 Nov: store, 3d guard: a hui promising the money kept whole is a Taiwan warning sign (law firm page, Banking Act not read); Book 19's guaranteed stays on the Treasuries, said beside what she owns.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3.0 evaluation: of l.11's two exclusions, a share price is Caplet's own and anybody else's money restates the case's rule (l.91-92) widened to every private promisor; Keel's reading, never a change to the IPS.

Tue 17 Nov: conceit candidate only: a hui sheet is a dated list all in pencil, Laura's ten the same list in ink; 3a's turn is already the one line that waited in pencil (CONCEIT V2.2), so an alternative to test in a voice round, never a second turn.

Tue 17 Nov: 3a or 3.0: say the 2003 survey alone with its limits (Lin 1985 is cited through Jou, row 14), keep the law's words, in words if 3a's three figures are full; never how Taiwanese hear anything.
Tue 17 Nov: 3d guard, consistent with SKELETON 3d: never name the hui in Laura's words; she is not Taiwanese (case p. 1) and funders are institutions (art. 709-2); she names what she owns.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: unlike a hui organiser, the extra Treasuries cover a gap with Laura's own 2028 money, so anybody else's money survives the backstop; no figure, names as WORDS sets them.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (1) and CANON B15: J.P. Morgan's 7.5% is unchanged a month on, read from a 7 Nov cached copy; re-read the live release before 27 Nov.
Tue 17 Nov: store, process: no new world-share figure from Q6b's fifteen houses 15-17 Nov; a search, not a census, and houses publish into December, so repeat by Thu 3 Dec.
Tue 17 Nov: store gap: BlackRock's updated assumptions are behind a professional wall; it sits at 9.0 and would need a fall over 1.5 points to drop below J.P. Morgan; read before 27 Nov.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (1) evidence: Goldman's 7.7% (Nov 2025) is a sixteenth house above J.P. Morgan, which is what makes upper third of published forecasts fragile; bank research, not an asset manager's assumption.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e area (1) evidence for row 8: with Goldman, five of sixteen are above J.P. Morgan, which ties sixth (median 6.7, Keel arithmetic checked on Q6b-022), just outside a strict upper third.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q6b-022 (twelve June-October 2026 figures, median 6.35, J.P. Morgan tied fourth); its new part, naming that panel if upper third is kept, is row 8's alternative.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: Morningstar, Verus and Schwab via a secondary aggregator, all below 7.5; never cited, Schwab conflicts with Q6b-021.

Tue 17 Nov: SKELETON 3e area (1), CANON B15 and the round-2 ban line: say above the middle of published forecasts; the median runs 6.35-6.7 by panel, so give about 6.5% only with the fifteen named, or drop it; never the top or the consensus.
Tue 17 Nov: 3e guard: Goldman's 2027 outlook gives one-year targets only; never set one beside a 10-15-year assumption or call it the newest forecast.
Tue 17 Nov: store gap: Morgan Stanley's seven-year 7.1% is the 2025 edition, outside Q6b's window; the 2026 figure is unread.
Tue 17 Nov: freshness check: VT's 30 Sep 2026 fact sheet is still the latest, so CANON B12-B14 stand word for word.
Tue 17 Nov: CANON B22 update for the lead: IBTM $640.1m on 16 Nov, 15 holdings, spread 0.05%, no notice; never quote its yield to maturity as the bottom, the payout is not fixed (B20).
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q45-017 (IBTR $112.3m, spread 0.04%, 4 holdings, 13 Nov); three days and $0.2m later, nothing new.

Tue 17 Nov: 2.2: closes SKELETON's re-read IBTR's holdings item, the Feb-2036 bond still held at 2.30% (13 Nov, was 3.03%); print the weight only with its date, and say IBTR holds a slice of it, never that the 2037 payment rests on it (Q93-014's guard).
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q3a-025 (the funds' not guaranteed and may experience losses wording, itself merged into Q16-001); recorded only as unchanged.
Tue 17 Nov: CANON B38 fix for the lead: the list misses IBGC (2046) and IBGM (2056), but no Treasury iBond fund ends 2037-2043, so 2.2's forced T-bonds for 2038-2042 stand.
Tue 17 Nov: 2.2 guard: BlackRock's 2037+ means a range running past 2037, not a 2037 Treasury fund; never quote it as one.
Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 row 4: no Treasury iBond fund ended early, merged or moved its end since August; IBTG follows its 15 Oct notice; never ended on schedule (IBTA ended 15 days early).
Tue 17 Nov: context only: NT$32.886 on 16 Nov, 0.36% weaker than NUMBERS 8d's 32.768 (Keel arithmetic checked); the register stays on 6 Nov and Table 3 row 7 measures from 2031.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q10c-019 (October CPI +2.33%, core +2.23%, next release 8 Dec 2026); still the latest, nothing new.

Tue 17 Nov: store, Table 3 row 7 context: October producer prices +19.66%, energy and chips, no building material named; the link to building costs is Keel inference, never a forecast that November's index rises.
Tue 17 Nov: context only: the 16 Nov curve is 0.20-0.32 points above 6 Nov at every tenor shown (checked against NUMBERS 0); direction only, never a re-priced plan figure.
Tue 17 Nov: store, 3e colour: the 6 Nov 10-year (4.86%) is the second-lowest close 23 Oct-16 Nov (23 Oct-6 Nov checked in the repo CSV); three weeks say nothing about January 2027.

Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 note for the exhibits owner: date today's rates once as the 6 Nov 2026 curve, as Table 2's note does; prose keeps WORDS' basis said once per part; the note's $38,282 and 3.60 points: check after tonight's re-size.

Tue 17 Nov: store: higher yields since 6 Nov widen, not narrow, Table 3's 3.60-point margin (direction only, NUMBERS 5); check after tonight's re-size, since the 0.5% margin on the payments moves that figure.

Tue 17 Nov: 3e clause or Table 2's note: auditing's subsequent-events rule (AS 2801) gives the frozen 6 Nov curve a reason, later market prices are disclosed, never re-booked; the sorting rule only, never audited figures.
Tue 17 Nov: store, beside row 26: AS 2801's pro forma form, a dated note beside the 6 Nov figures and never a silent swap, if a reviewer insists on newer rates.
Tue 17 Nov: store only: AS 2905 covers facts that existed but were found later (the Goldman case); from advisory slides, not the standard's text.

Tue 17 Nov: Table 3 note and 3e area (4): Taiwan's next CPI and building-cost readings land 8 Dec, after the 5 Dec deadline, so October 2026 is the last citable reading; check DGBAS's outlook on Thu 3 Dec.
Tue 17 Nov: twin of Q10-016 (DGBAS 2.07% and 1.90%, central bank 2.03% and 1.83%); confirmed still the latest, nothing new.
